home.name: Francis Desjardins
home.enough: A dependency is easy to add and hard to remove, and most of what one does goes unused. The cost of adding one never arrives on the day you add it.

skills.title: What I build
skills.description: Writing code since high school, for a living since 2000. The layer I keep coming back to sits between a client and a server: a proprietary communication protocol, a real-time client-server layer, interfaces between processes, and the test benches that hold them.
skills.habits: Two habits came out of it. Cores that reach no framework, with thin bindings over them: plain TypeScript that runs in a browser, a worker or a service, and a test that fails if the core ever reaches a framework. And protocols written down first, then built to the letter in every language that speaks them.
skills.thinking: A state library and a draft engine, to hold a few plain objects, is a cannon aimed at a fly: a set of listeners and a shallow compare do the same work, nine kilobytes lighter. Some problems are the other way round — time zones, cryptography, anything whose hard part is the one you have not met yet. Between the two, a library earns its place the day the requirements outgrow what you wrote.
skills.secondary: Also: a self-declared cat person. The cats have yet to object. And I delegate to AI agents; one of them is there to disagree with the others.

work.title: What's running
work.description: Four pieces, each with a surface you can try. The names come from an eclipse: the beads of light that break through at its edge, and the three shadows it casts. What they refuse to do is documented as carefully as the rest.

dialog.name: antumbra
dialog.description: Dialog manager on the native top layer. Zero shipped UI: the renderer stays yours. React, Solid and vanilla bindings.

boot.name: umbra
boot.description: Bootstrap orchestration, and not a front-end kind: the core needs no DOM, so one declared graph boots a page, a worker or a service. You say what each step needs; the parallelism is derived from that — no flag, no concurrency ceiling.

designSystem.name: penumbra
designSystem.description: The design system all four playgrounds wear — and the page that takes it apart, one layer at a time.

bead.name: Bead
bead.description: A binary call protocol, specification first. TypeScript and C# at parity, with Rust on the way: each plays the same conformance files, and they call each other in CI over WebSocket, HTTP, MQTT 5 and AMQP 1.0. A builder generates a typed server and its client from a .proto. Here the server runs in a Web Worker of the page.

location.since: Breathing air since the early eighties

home.title: Francis Desjardins: framework-free libraries, and Bead, a binary call protocol
home.description: Framework-free cores with thin bindings over them: the core is plain TypeScript that runs in a browser, a worker or a service, and the binding is the only part that knows which. Three libraries with no runtime dependencies between them, and Bead, a binary call protocol in TypeScript and C#.
home.ogTitle: Francis Desjardins: framework-free libraries, and Bead, a binary call protocol
home.ogDescription: A dependency is easy to add and hard to remove, and most of what one does goes unused. Three libraries that ship none, a binary call protocol in two languages, and the measured reason why.
